analysis_plan.generalisation: Each selected router is scored on BOTH yardsticks on both blocks. An objective is said to generalise only if it is competitive on the yardstick it was not selected for.
analysis_plan.no_single_winner_claim: No claim of the form 'objective X is best' will be made from a single yardstick, since each objective is advantaged on its own.
analysis_plan.null_handling: Null and inconclusive results are recorded as measured and are not re-run, re-seeded, or re-thresholded, per POC_PLAN.md.
analysis_plan.primary: For each selected router, the paired regret delta against the random baseline per family, computed independently on block A and block B, with 95% bootstrap intervals. The replication rule decides what counts as a result.

claim_boundary: Synthetic landscape comparison of three selection objectives for one exploitation rule. Not evidence about model self-improvement or a recursive effect.

instrument.seed_disjointness: E59/E60 used 0-239 and E61 used 1000-1239. E62 uses 2000-2119 for selection and 3000-3119 / 4000-4119 for the two held-out blocks, all mutually disjoint.

objectives.macro_mean: minimise the unweighted mean regret across admitted families
objectives.signal_weighted: minimise mean regret weighted by each family's policy-disagreement rate, so families where policies can barely differ contribute little. The weights come from the admission sweep and are a property of the cohort, never of the candidate under test.
objectives.worst_family: minimise the worst admitted family's mean regret; the objective E59 and E60 used without comparison

predictions.basis: worst-family is maximin and macro-mean is an average; E61 showed they disagree sharply on monotone.
predictions.statement: The three objectives do not all select the same router.

predictions.basis: E61 measured a threefold gap on monotone between E41's gate and E60's worst-family selection.
predictions.statement: The worst-family-selected router is beaten on macro-mean regret by at least one other objective's router, on both blocks.

predictions.basis: E41's (0.5, 0.01) gate dominated on monotone in E61, so an objective that rewards signal should recover something like it.
predictions.statement: At least one objective selects a router with an R^2 threshold of 0.5 or higher, i.e. a genuinely support-aware gate.

predictions.basis: A stability check on the methodology itself. If two disjoint blocks disagree on the ranking, single-block selection in this benchmark is unsound and the replication rule is load-bearing.
predictions.statement: The ranking of the three selected routers by macro-mean regret is identical on block A and block B.

predictions.basis: Speculative, and a direct test of whether the replication rule earns its cost. E60's rugged result behaved exactly this way across E60 and E61.
predictions.statement: At least one per-family effect clears in one block and fails to replicate in the other.

question: Does any promotion objective generalise beyond the yardstick it was selected for, and does worst-family selection give up a replicated advantage on the families that carry signal?
replication_rule: An effect is a result only if block A and block B agree in sign, both 95% bootstrap intervals exclude zero, and both point estimates clear the minimum effect size. Agreement in one block only is reported as unreplicated and is not counted as a finding.
